title: Deep Learning with INT8 Optimization on Xilinx Devices (WP486 v1.0.1)
notes: Two INT8 MACs per DSP48E2 sharing one operand (a<<18 + b packed via pre-adder, times shared 8-bit c); accumulation of up to 7 product terms guaranteed without lower-term overflow; 8 DSPs do 7x2 MACs -> 1.75x; UINT8 activations -> 1.78x (pp.3-5, 7). Peak GOPS/W bar chart (Fig. 8) is for Kintex/Virtex devices, not recorded.

title: 8-Bit Dot-Product Acceleration (WP487 v1.0)
notes: INT8: a<<18 on port A, d on port D, shared b on port B (G=18); P[17:0]=d.b, a.b = P[35:18] + P[17] (increment only on the final packed word); N<=7 terms per 18-bit field; 8 DSPs -> 14 MACs (1.75x) or 2x with LUT incrementer/adders. UINT8 x INT8: G=19, bias removed via port C/WMUX, N<=8, 16/9 = 1.78x (pp.6-14).

title: DSP-Packing: Squeezing Low-precision Arithmetic into FPGA DSP Blocks
notes: Generalises Xilinx INT8/INT4 packing (INT-N); extraction by right shift floors -> error -1 (Xilinx INT4: MAE 0.37, error probability 37.35%, WCE 1). Full correction (round-half-up) MAE 0 with 27 LUT + 32 FF; approximate correction via port C: EP 3.13%, 0 LUT. With delta padding bits up to 2^delta results can be accumulated without error. Overpacking (delta<0) is approximate.
